description:
We are a student team working on ISPSC-Intelligent System for Predicting Suitable Crops, a smart agriculture project that aims to help farmers make better decisions and improve food security

Our project combines NASA Earth observation data, AI, data analysis, and IoT soil sensors to evaluate agricultural conditions and recommend the most suitable crops based on climate and soil characteristics.

We are passionate about technology, innovation, scientific research, and solving real-world problems
summary:
ISPSC – Intelligent System for Predicting Suitable Crops

ISPSC is an intelligent agricultural decision-support system designed to help farmers select the most suitable crops for their land under changing environmental and climate conditions. The project combines NASA Earth observation and climate data with soil measurements collected through a smart soil-analysis device. It uses these inputs alongside a database of more than 200 crops to evaluate soil properties, temperature requirements, and growing conditions.
The system aims to provide farmers with ranked crop recommendations, suitability scores, and explanations of potential risks and limiting factors. It also supports better crop rotation planning and more informed agricultural decisions. By connecting NASA data, real-world soil measurements, and crop requirements, ISPSC addresses the Field Shift challenge and aims to help farmers adapt to environmental changes, use agricultural resources more efficiently, and make data-driven decisions.
details:
ISPSC – Intelligent System for Predicting Suitable Crops

ISPSC is an intelligent agricultural decision-support platform developed to help farmers make better crop-selection decisions based on the actual environmental and soil conditions of their farms. It combines satellite-based and climate information from NASA with field measurements collected using a smart soil-analysis device.

How the System Works

The process begins when a farmer selects a farm location and provides its basic information. The platform uses the farm's location to retrieve relevant environmental and climate data from NASA sources. A connected soil-analysis device then collects soil measurements, including parameters such as soil temperature, moisture, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and nutrient indicators (NPK), depending on the available sensor readings.

The device is built around an ESP32 microcontroller and communicates with a 7-in-1 soil sensor through an RS485 interface. The collected measurements are sent to the system for storage and analysis.

ISPSC then evaluates the farm conditions using an existing database containing more than 200 crops and their growing requirements. The analysis compares soil properties, temperature ranges, and other available environmental factors with each crop's suitability conditions. The system can then rank crop options and provide suitability scores, explanations, and potential limitations to help farmers understand why a crop may or may not be suitable.

Technology and Development

The project combines a web platform developed using React and JavaScript, a backend and database powered by Supabase and PostgreSQL, a mobile application developed with Flutter and Dart, and an ESP32-based hardware prototype programmed using Arduino/C++. These components are intended to connect environmental data, real soil measurements, crop information, and farmer-facing recommendations in one workflow.

Innovation and Impact

The main innovation of ISPSC is connecting large-scale Earth observation data with measurements taken directly from the farm and a structured crop database. Instead of relying only on general agricultural recommendations, the platform aims to provide location-specific, data-driven guidance. Its intended impact is to support better crop selection, improve agricultural resource management, reduce unsuitable planting decisions, and help farmers adapt to changing climate and environmental conditions. ISPSC is being developed as a practical prototype, with continued testing and improvement of data integration, sensor accuracy, and crop-analysis reliability.
projectRefs: A comprehensive crop database integrating climate needs, salinity limits, and production costs; used as our core reference library to match with NASA data for predicting the best crop for any land.
